podcast.title: Alcohol Abuse and Band Tensions
podcast.body: By 1998, after three straight years of intense touring with little time off, Scott's drinking problems became severe, leading to escalating tensions, fights, and a breakdown in communication among band members. "But his problems with drinking continued, something had to give."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 1

podcast.title: Bedroom Recording Studio
podcast.body: His bedroom served as the primary recording venue for Blink's early demo tapes, including "Fly Swatter" and "Demo Number Two," where a mix of original songs and covers were produced. "It was a mix of original songs and covers recorded in Scott's bedroom that was distributed on cassette."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 1

podcast.title: Disagreement over Major Label Deal
podcast.body: He strongly believed that signing with MCA, a major label, constituted a "very unpunk move," creating significant friction and disagreement within the band, particularly with Mark Hoppas and Tom DeLong who were supportive of the deal. "Scott? Not so much. He thought that signing with MCA was a very unpunk move."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 1

podcast.title: Family Relocation and Living Arrangements
podcast.body: His family moved to Reno, Nevada, which created a logistical challenge for him to participate in recording "Cheshire Cat" with the band. To overcome this, he moved in with his sister in San Diego temporarily. "To make matters even more complicated, Scott's family had just moved to Reno, Nevada. So he moved in with his sister in San Diego while the band made the record."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 1

podcast.title: Fired from Blink-182
podcast.body: In May 1998, despite agreeing to enter rehab, Tom DeLong and Mark Hoppas felt that Scott's behavior was negatively impacting the band's performances, leading to his dismissal. While some accounts suggest he was fired over the phone, he was ultimately replaced by Travis Barker. "So Scott was fired. Some story said he was fired over the phone, but whatever the case is, he was out and Travis was in."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 1

podcast.title: Initial Meeting with Tom DeLong
podcast.body: Scott Rainer, a drummer whose current band was "falling apart," was drawn to Tom DeLong's solo acoustic performance at a local battle of the bands. He later met Tom at a party, which eventually led to their musical collaboration. "And this attracted the attention of a drummer named Scott Rainer who was in a band that was in the process of falling apart."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 1

podcast.title: Temporary Replacement by Mark Crawl
podcast.body: Due to ongoing issues with his living arrangements, Scott was temporarily replaced by his high school friend, Mark Crawl. During this period, the band pooled money to facilitate Scott's travel back and forth between Reno and San Diego. "For a while, the band pulled money so we could fly back and forth to Reno. And for a time, he was replaced by a dude named Mark Crawl, who was Scott's high school buddy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 1

podcast.title: Underage for Contract
podcast.body: When Blink signed with Cargo Records, Scott was under the age of 18, making him legally ineligible to sign the contract himself. "The only member of the band who could sign the contract was Mark. He was old enough. Tom wasn't around because he was work and Scott was under 18, so he was ineligible."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 1

podcast.title: Unfinished High School and College Thoughts
podcast.body: Due to his commitments with the band, Scott never completed high school. Around the time of his departure from Blink-182, he began to consider attending college, indicating a period of personal conflict and reflection. "Even though because of his work with a man, he never even finished high school."

xref.title: Learning Blink-182 Songs Quickly
xref.body: According to legend, Travis Barker impressively learned the drum parts for 20 Blink-182 songs in just 45 minutes when he was asked to temporarily fill in for Scott Rainer. "Legend says that he learned his parts to 20 Blink 182 songs in 45 minutes. That's pretty impressive."

xref.title: Lending Travis Barker to Blink
xref.body: The Aquabats displayed remarkable cooperation by "really cool"ly lending their drummer, Travis Barker, to Blink when Scott Rainer needed to return to California. "When Scott Rainer had to go back to California, the Aquabats were really cool in lending Travis to Blink."

xref.title: Previous Bands and Connection to Tom
xref.body: Before joining Blink, Mark, who was a few years older than Tom DeLong and Scott Rainer, had already been a member of "a bunch of bands." He connected with Tom through his sister, who was dating one of Tom's friends, leading to their collaboration in songwriting. "Mark's sister was going out with one of Tom's friends, a connection was made and they started writing songs together."

xref.title: Scott Rainer's Broken Heels
xref.body: During the recording sessions for "Dude Ranch," drummer Scott Rainer, under the influence of alcohol, believed he could fly and jumped off an unspecified object, resulting in him breaking both his heels. Consequently, he recorded most of his drum parts while in a wheelchair or on crutches. "One night Scott got a little drunk and was convinced he could fly. So he jumped off something and broke both his heels."
